headline: How the position ends matters only for strategies that realize gains, and it never rescues one. If the position ends in a step-up at death or a gift of appreciated shares, instead of the protocol's full liquidation, the 2x SMA175/3% conditional lead loses its California support: boot_p goes from 0.077 to 0.199 (2000-26) and from 0.067 to 0.219 (1986-2026), and the worst 10-year window turns negative. Under a 20-year sale in retirement it is borderline (p 0.110 / 0.120). The r2_lev2x round-2 pick fails too (p 0.097 -> 0.215; its FED 1930-85 pass breaks, 0.074 -> 0.118). Frozen tax-managed books barely move, every other verdict stands, and nothing new passes. SPY buy-and-hold remains the default; for a hold-until-death investor the protocol understates SPY's edge over a realizing strategy by about 1.3-1.5 pp/yr per unit of annual realization.

recommendation.label: Verified CONDITIONAL lead, re-scored by how the position ends: 2x S&P (SSO-like) while SPY > SMA175 with a 3% band, checked daily and traded at the close, else VFITX/IEF. This is NOT a good-confidence pass. SPY buy-and-hold remains the default for the CA taxable account.

long_r.history: 1986-2026, repaired VFINX world, validated simulator (matches the engine to <0.001 pp per window)

numbers.neighbourhood: Daily grid of 54 2x configs (SMA 100-300 x band 0-5%), counting configs that pass items 1-3. Under liquidation: 2 on 2000-26 and 4 on 1986-2026. Under the step-up: 0 in every history. Under the retirement sale: 1 and 1, not the same config. Item 5 therefore fails for the 2x lead under every non-liquidation ending.

risks: If the account ends in a step-up or a gift, the CA excess is about +3.7 to +4.2 pp/yr in the modern histories with p of about 0.2. The worst 10-year window is -1.5 to -1.8 pp/yr, and there is no significance before 1986 (p 0.33).

All of the verify_lev_robust risks still apply: post-hoc parameters (DSR about 0.004, PBO about 0.5-0.6); the one-day-lag fragility (1987, -59% drawdown); the 1930-85 holdout is not significant; a 10-32% bootstrapped chance of trailing SPY over 20 years; and the edge depends on multi-month trend persistence.

Under liquidation accounting the after-tax monthly volatility of a fresh 2x lot is damped by the 48.1% short-term rate. A holder who never sells sees the undamped volatility (23.6% vs 15.5% on 2000-26), which is part of why its p-value rises.
conditions: Only for a CA investor who expects to liquidate the account, or sell it down within about 10 years at long-term rates. Under those endings boot_p stays at or below 0.10 on 2000-26 and 1986-2026.

Not for a buy-hold-until-death or charitable-gift plan. There SPY buy-and-hold is preferred: its embedded gain (24.7% of value on 2000-26) is forgiven, while the 2x rule has already paid 520k of its 1,767k ending equity in tax along the way, plus 6.3% for 2026.
In FED (35/15) the lead keeps p at or below 0.10 under every ending on 2000-26 and 1986-2026.
It has to be executed at the same close as the signal, with a 2x daily-reset fund (SSO).

alternatives.label: SPY buy-and-hold (the default)
alternatives.note: By definition 0 excess under every ending. Under a step-up or gift its after-tax value equals its pre-tax value. The protocol's liquidation charges it 24.7% of its 2000-26 value (15.1% under the 20-year sale at g=7%). Control: SPY sold and re-bought every 366 days scores -1.13 (liquidation), -2.43 (step-up) and -1.41 (20-year sale) pp/yr in CA on 2000-26, and -1.24 / -2.69 / -1.51 on 1986-2026.
alternatives.confidence: high that nothing tested beats it with good confidence under any ending

alternatives.label: KX3, the round-1 unlevered best (378-0 momentum, top 5, semiannual, 1% budget, K-execution)
alternatives.verdict: Unchanged: FAIL on items 4, 6 and 7. The ending barely matters for a frozen book, and the start-date artifact dominates.

alternatives.label: C1: 3x SMA175/3% daily, the round-1 leveraged lead
alternatives.verdict: Unchanged: FAIL (tail risk of -88 to -93% drawdowns, post hoc). It now also fails items 1-3 under a step-up on 2000-26.

alternatives.label: r2_lev2x pick S200|A2|IEF|D-h1: 2x SSO / IEF, SMA200 3% band, daily, 60-day short-term deferral
alternatives.verdict: Fails in CA under every ending. Its FED all-history pass does not survive a step-up.

alternatives.label: r2_lev2x CU.5: core 0.5 SPY never sold + UPRO / IEF sleeve, SMA175 3% band
alternatives.verdict: Passes all four histories only under liquidation. Its drawdown (-57% vs SPY -55% after 1986) is the reason r2_lev2x excluded it. The never-sold core keeps the step-up cost small (-0.24 to -0.43 score), but p still fails on 2000-26 and 1930-85.

alternatives.label: Exploratory (simulator): never-sold S&P core 50% + 3x SMA175/3% sleeve
alternatives.verdict: Pointer only, not a candidate: post-hoc sleeve and 3x tail risk. A never-sold core cuts the step-up penalty from about 0.8-0.95 to 0.2-0.55 pp/yr, but none of these structures passes every history under a step-up.

findings: The method is exact. TermGate, a core.Gate subclass in families/r2_gap4.py, values the engine's own FIFO lots, realized-gain buckets and carryforward at every checkpoint and month end, under each ending: liquidation, pre-liquidation equity, step-up, donation, and a 20-year minimum-tax sale for 6 combinations of growth g and years N. Its liquidation and equity values equal the lab's cached values at all 725,423 checkpoints of the 135 cached (config, regime) records (relative difference 0.0). Sanity: SPY run as a strategy shows 0.00 excess under every ending. The extended single-lot simulator matches the engine to <0.001 pp in every window for 3 leveraged configs.

The protocol's liquidation convention has two opposite biases. It charges SPY's deferred gain in full: 24.7% of its 2000-26 value, which a step-up removes and a 20-year sale shrinks to a 15.1% haircut. That favours realizers. It also taxes realizers' lots younger than a year at short-term rates, which penalizes them slightly: the 2x lead scores +5.18 when every lot is taxed at long-term rates, against +4.94. The first bias dominates for anyone holding to a step-up, and for 20-year sales at g >= about 4%.

Pure realization cost, measured on SPY itself (CA, 2000-26 score). Sold and re-bought every 366 days: -1.13 under liquidation, -2.43 under a step-up, -1.41 under the 20-year sale. Every 182 days: -3.01 / -4.84 / -3.61. On 1986-2026: -1.24 / -2.69 / -1.51. For a hold-until-death investor the protocol understates SPY's advantage by about 1.3-1.5 pp/yr per unit of annual realization.

Across 108 finalists (CA, 2000-26), the step-up changes the score by a median of -0.50 pp/yr (range -2.49 to +0.59; FED median -0.15). The change tracks turnover, Spearman -0.88. By turnover per year: below 0.15, +0.05; 0.15-0.5, -0.62; 0.5-1, -1.04; above 1, -1.37. The 20-year sale changes the score by a median of -0.02 (range -0.86 to +0.53).

Configs passing bar items 1-3 (CA / FED): liquidation 25 / 31; step-up 14 / 23 (11 / 8 lose the pass, none gain); donation is the same as the step-up; 20-year sale at g=7% 25 / 30 (3 lose and 3 gain in CA, all on thresholds and all failing other items).

2x SMA175/3% conditional lead, CA. Under a step-up, p goes from 0.077 to 0.199 (2000-26) and from 0.067 to 0.219 (1986-2026); score from +4.94 to +4.18 and from +4.62 to +3.73; the worst 10y window from +0.6 to -1.5 pp/yr. It is still positive in every 20-year window in the modern histories (mean +3.6 / +3.8, overlapping windows). Under the 20-year sale p is 0.110 / 0.120; it is at or below 0.10 only if g <= 4% or N <= 10. On 1930-85, p is 0.27 (liquidation) and 0.33 (step-up). In FED it holds: step-up p 0.091 / 0.048.

The step-up hurts the 2x lead's p for two reasons. The mean monthly excess falls (+3.47 to +2.65 pp/yr). The tracking error rises (14.4% to 19.5%), because liquidation accounting damps a young 2x lot's after-tax swings by the 48.1% short-term rate.

The neighbourhood (daily grid, CA) collapses under a step-up. No 2x config passes items 1-3 in any history, against 2 on 2000-26 and 4 on 1986-2026 under liquidation. Configs passing both modern histories: 13 under liquidation, 1 under a step-up, 7 (all 3x) under the 20-year sale. Configs passing all four histories: 1 under liquidation, 0 under a step-up.

Round-2 r2_lev2x designs, re-scored with r2_lev2x's own configs; the liquidation numbers match its report exactly. The pick goes from p 0.097 to 0.215 under a step-up on 2000-26 and also fails the 10y/15y beat rates (0.58 / 0.75); on 1986-2026, 0.070 to 0.195. Its FED 1930-85 pass breaks (0.074 to 0.118). CU.5 (never-sold core plus UPRO sleeve) passes all four histories under liquidation but fails 2000-26 (0.119) and 1930-85 (0.178) under a step-up.

Frozen tax-managed books barely move. KX3 score: +0.99 liquidation, +1.06 step-up, +1.16 20-year sale. Site preset: +0.66 / +0.69 / +0.82. Their verdicts (FAIL on items 4, 6 and 7) are unchanged. Start dependence is far bigger than the ending: KX3's boot_p from the 2000-01 start is 0.011, but averaged over the five yearly starts 2000-2004 it is 0.25-0.29 under every ending.

Unlevered timing rules, TAA, macro curve rules, volatility targeting, seasonal, global and the 3x family all keep their FAIL verdicts. The step-up widens their margins: EMA100/200 +1.01 to +0.61, uninv540 full excess +3.76 to +2.61 (p 0.064 to 0.188), GATED p 0.101 to 0.272, TAA rules -1.3 to -1.7. All long_r twins fail under every ending.

The critic's cache-only proxy (pre-liquidation equity) reproduces exactly but omits the tax still owed on gains realized earlier in the same year, so it understated the step-up penalty for realizers. For C1 the proxy shows the score rising to +9.85, but the exact step-up gives +9.33. For the 2x lead: +4.60 (proxy) vs +4.18 (exact). Donation is within 0.17 pp of the step-up everywhere.

Exploratory, 48 simulator runs: a never-sold S&P core with a 3x trend sleeve keeps more of the edge under a step-up. Its score cost is 0.2-0.55 pp/yr, against 0.76-0.95 for the all-in 2x. No such structure passes every history under a step-up, and the 3x sleeves add tail risk.
concerns: The step-up and gift endings assume current US law (IRC 1014 basis step-up, a charitable deduction at market value for long-term lots). Estate tax, AGI limits on gifts and future law changes are not modelled. Estate tax is roughly proportional to value, so it nearly cancels in a CAGR comparison.

The retirement sale freezes both books at the window's end. A strategy that kept trading would realize more, so the ending is generous to realizers. It gives every holding the same post-window growth g, also used as the discount rate, and reports a cash-equivalent value. Results depend on g and N (2x lead, 2000-26 CA: p 0.073 at g=0 up to 0.121 at N=30).
Every ending is applied at every window end, including 5-year windows. That is a 'what if it ended here' scoring, not a probability-weighted expectation of when an investor dies or retires.

Within each window the engine sells FIFO. Only the post-window sale uses minimum-tax lot order; specific-lot selling during the window is gap5's question. Engine limits are inherited: dividends and interest are taxed as deferred gains, FED omits the 3.8% NIIT, and wash sales are not enforced (immaterial for these single-asset switches).
boot_p comes from the first start's monthly path. The 5-start averages I report are much less favourable for KX3, the incumbent and the 2x lead under every ending.

The 1930-2026 and 1986-2026 leveraged results come from verify_lev_robust's single-lot simulator, extended here. It is validated against the engine on 2000-26 for every ending, not re-validated on the older data; the pre-1986 world uses approximate dividends and T-bill rates.

Configs: 149 configs evaluated under 10 endings each. They are 109 on full; 11 long_r twins; 15 r2_lev2x configs; 8 leveraged rules x 4 histories (simulator); and 6 core+sleeve structures x 4 histories (simulator). Separately, the 162-config daily leverage grid x 4 histories was re-scored. Only about 10 are new strategies (4 churn controls, 5 core+sleeve structures, the real-SSO 2x trend rule); the rest re-score existing paths, so the deflated-Sharpe trial count rises only to about 12,500.

Other round-2 results (combos, rotation_final, gap1-3, gap5, gap6) were not published when this finished, so only r2_lev2x's designs were re-scored. The results file gives a five-line recipe (G.run_terms + G.summary) to re-score any later finalist.
